context: The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection is Rockstar's first large physical product for GTA VI, and it surfaced in an unusual way. On September 24, Insider Gaming reported that a datamined list of 55 Rockstar Store items included the box, possibly limited to one per person; Rockstar opened pre-orders the same day.

It sits outside the two game editions Rockstar announced in June: the $79.99 Standard Edition and the $99.99 Ultimate Edition, with pre-orders that opened on June 25. Unlike the collector's editions of many big releases, the box contains no copy of the game and no download code. Reports say deliveries are due to start around the November 19 launch, with shipping and import duties charged separately.
known: The box costs $399.99, £349.99 or €399.99 and is sold through the Rockstar Store.
It does not include GTA VI or a download code; the game is sold separately.
Headline items are a six-inch Macca the Gator figure with a twist-open stash base, Oakley Frogskins sunglasses with Prizm Sapphire lenses, a New Era 9FORTY cap and a Leonida Keys crossbody bag.
Smaller items include nine enamel pins in a metal tin, a sticker pack and a double-sided poster with a map of Leonida.
Guru3D reports a limit of one box per customer, matching what the earlier datamine suggested.
unknown: Rockstar has not said how many boxes were made or whether there will be restocks.
Exact delivery dates by region are unclear; reports only place the first shipments around launch.
It is not confirmed whether the poster map shows Leonida exactly as it appears in the final game.
The datamined list had 55 store items, and Rockstar has not said when, or whether, the rest will go on sale.
take: Four hundred dollars for merchandise without the game is a hard sell, and the reaction in Push Square's comments was mostly negative. Much of the value rests on the Oakleys and the New Era cap, branded items with appeal outside GTA. The rest is souvenir material: shot glass, swizzle spoon, mirror, keychain. Within a day, fans were sharing 3D-printable files of the Macca figure, which says a lot about how much of the price is the logo.

For most players the practical point is simpler. This is not a collector's edition in the usual sense, and pairing it with the Standard Edition comes to roughly $480 before shipping and taxes. The razor-blade keychain and the hidden stash fit Rockstar's satirical tone, though they also make this an adult collectible rather than a gift for younger fans. If the box sells out quickly despite the price, expect more premium merchandise around launch; if it lingers, that would be a rare sign of where GTA fans draw the line.

titulo: Is the GTA 6 Map Bigger Than Leonida? An Old Puerto Rico Rumor Resurfaces After the 192GB Leak
texto: Ever since the 192GB archive of old Rockstar material surfaced online on September 18, 2026, fans have been combing through early GTA 6 map files, which Kotaku dates to around 2015 (only MMOCulture mentions 2014). Among the theories spreading in the community, an old one has resurfaced: a fan rumor, first posted on 4chan in 2021, about an island inspired by **Puerto Rico**, which would point to a playable area outside the state of Leonida. The idea is not new for the series. In GTA 5, the snowy town of North Yankton appeared only in specific story missions, far from Los Santos. Fans suggest a Caribbean island could play a similar role in GTA 6, especially because of Lucia's Latin roots. Here is what we know, and what we don't: - **What is confirmed:** Rockstar has only officially presented the state of Leonida, with six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and Mount Kalaga. - **What the leak shows:** Outlets that analysed the archive describe an early Leonida prototype, with labels such as "Alligator Farm", "Coast Guard" and "Disused Theme Park", plus early Vice City assets. - **What remains unverified:** None of the outlets we checked mention a Puerto Rico-style island. The theory is an old fan rumor from 2021, not something found in the leaked files. - **Why caution matters:** The files are about a decade old. take: We don't consider the island theory a credible guide to the final game. titulo: 192GB Rockstar Leak Surfaces: Cancelled GTA 5 Liberty City DLC, Agent Trevor and Early GTA 6 Assets
texto: About 192GB of internal Rockstar Games data surfaced online on September 18, 2026, two months before the launch of GTA 6. The files are not new: they are linked to the security breach Rockstar suffered in 2022, part of which had already leaked as GTA 5 source code in December 2023. The full archive circulated privately for years and has only now been shared widely. Despite the timing, most of the material is about **GTA 5**, not GTA 6. Dataminers in the community, such as TJGM, have been sharing their findings, though many of them have not been independently verified. Check out the main highlights reported so far: - **Cancelled Liberty City expansion for GTA 5:** Files for a single-player DLC that would have brought Liberty City to GTA 5, with a map reportedly larger than the version seen in GTA 4. - **"Agent Trevor" DLC:** A cancelled secret-agent expansion starring Trevor, with dozens of missions and assets that include spaceship interiors and space suits. - **Cut endings and missions:** An alternate, more brutal death for Trevor in one of GTA 5's endings, and a cut mission pairing Franklin with Brucie, the GTA 4 character. - **Beta content:** Dialogue and vehicles from GTA 5's development that never made it into the final game. - **Early GTA 6 assets:** Very early, low-detail models and map blockouts of Vice City and Leonida, dated to around 2014–2015 and reportedly built with GTA 5's tools. That last point is what drew the most attention, but it says little about the game coming in November. As the coverage of the leak stresses, blockouts this old do not represent the final map, which has been rebuilt many times since. Following our editorial policy, we report that the leak happened, but we do not show or link to the leaked material. Rockstar has not commented on this archive. GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges!

The full archive circulated privately for years and has only now been shared widely.

Despite the timing, most of the material is about GTA 5, not GTA 6. Dataminers in the community, such as TJGM, have been sharing their findings, though many of them have not been independently verified.

Check out the main highlights reported so far:

  • Cancelled Liberty City expansion for GTA 5:
    Files for a single-player DLC that would have brought Liberty City to GTA 5, with a map reportedly larger than the version seen in GTA 4.

  • "Agent Trevor" DLC:
    A cancelled secret-agent expansion starring Trevor, with dozens of missions and assets that include spaceship interiors and space suits.

  • Cut endings and missions:
    An alternate, more brutal death for Trevor in one of GTA 5's endings, and a cut mission pairing Franklin with Brucie, the GTA 4 character.

  • Beta content:
    Dialogue and vehicles from GTA 5's development that never made it into the final game.

  • Early GTA 6 assets:
    Very early, low-detail models and map blockouts of Vice City and Leonida, dated to around 2014–2015 and reportedly built with GTA 5's tools.

That last point is what drew the most attention, but it says little about the game coming in November. As the coverage of the leak stresses, blockouts this old do not represent the final map, which has been rebuilt many times since.

Following our editorial policy, we report that the leak happened, but we do not show or link to the leaked material. Rockstar has not commented on this archive. GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

titulo: Stephen Root Confirms He's in GTA 6, Widely Believed to Voice Brian Heder: "You're Gonna See Me in There"
texto: American actor **Stephen Root** has confirmed that he is in Grand Theft Auto VI, making him the first member of the cast to publicly go on record about a role in the game. He did not name his character, but fans and the press, who recognized his voice, widely believe he plays **Brian Heder**. Root spoke to the Associated Press at the BAFTA TV Tea Party in mid-September 2026. Asked about GTA 6, he did not dodge the question: "You're gonna see me in there." He also admitted that keeping the secret had become almost impossible, because fans had already recognized him: "There were too many people that knew me from King of the Hill and my voice." Check out what we know about the actor and his character: - **Who is Brian Heder:** According to Rockstar's official profile, Brian is an old-school drug runner in the Leonida Keys who lets Jason live in one of his properties in exchange for help with his business. In other words, he is one of the first people players will meet, since the story begins in the Keys. - **Who is Stephen Root:** A veteran character actor known as Milton in *Office Space*, Monroe Fuches in *Barry*, and the voices of Bill Dauterive and Buck Strickland in the animated series *King of the Hill*. - **How fans found out:** Players began linking the voice to Root as soon as Brian was introduced in the second trailer, in May 2025. The Extended Look shown in August 2026 gave him more screen time and turned the guess into near-certainty. - **What is still a secret:** Rockstar has not officially announced the cast, and the actors behind Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos remain unconfirmed. Root's comments suggest the studio is relaxing its famously tight secrecy as launch approaches. More cast reveals, official or not, are likely in the coming weeks. Meet the rest of the characters in our guide: [Jason, Lucia and the GTA 6 cast](https://vvviceversa.com/guides/gta-6-characters-jason-lucia/). GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges! *Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article said Stephen Root confirmed he plays Brian Heder. In fact, Root confirmed he is in the game but did not name his character; the link to Brian Heder comes from fans and the press, who recognized his voice.*

context: Rockstar has never published a cast list for GTA VI, so Stephen Root's remarks to the Associated Press are the first time an actor has publicly placed himself in the game. Speaking at the BAFTA Tea Party in Beverly Hills, in the same stretch in which he won an Emmy for Apple TV's Widow's Bay, Root said: "Yeah, you're gonna see me in there." He added that his character had been part of the game's first rollout almost a year earlier.

Fans had tied Brian Heder's voice to Root since the character appeared in the second trailer on May 6, 2025. Root did not say the name himself. The Brian Heder link comes from that fan identification, which Variety and other outlets now treat as settled.
known: Root told the AP he appears in GTA VI and that online sleuths had recognized his voice, which many people know from King of the Hill.
Rockstar's character guide describes Brian Heder as a classic drug runner from the golden age of smuggling in the Keys, still moving product through his boatyard with his third wife, Lori.
Brian appears in the Extended Look meeting Jason and Lucia at a rooftop party and sharing a cigar with Jason.
Root was born and raised in Florida and studied at the University of Florida, according to Variety.
Rockstar has not officially named any cast member and did not comment on Root's remarks.
unknown: Root did not say which character he plays, and Rockstar has not confirmed that he voices Brian Heder.
The actors behind Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos have not been revealed.
The size of Brian's role in the story is unknown beyond his link to Jason in the Keys.
Rockstar has not said whether it will share cast details before the November 19 launch.
take: The Brian Heder identification is about as close to certain as it gets without Rockstar's word. Root confirmed he is in the game, placed his character in the first wave of promotion and pointed to the King of the Hill voice that gave him away, and no other character from those trailers has been tied to him. Still, the specific claim rests on inference. Headlines saying he confirmed the name go one step further than he did.

The more telling part is that he spoke at all. Rockstar has kept GTA VI's cast off the record through two trailers and the Extended Look, and an Emmy winner talking openly to a wire service suggests that wall is getting harder to hold this close to launch. The casting also fits the role Rockstar describes: Root's best-known work, from Barry to King of the Hill, leans on comic, slightly shady characters, and he has real Florida roots. Watch for more actors to talk as launch nears, though the leads are the reveals that matter.

titulo: GTA 6 Daily Life Detailed: A Physical Phone, a Shared Hideout and Protected Story Locations
texto: With 65 days to go until launch, Rockstar keeps revealing how life in Leonida will work between missions. In a long interview with the Japanese magazine **Famitsu**, translated into English by GTAVice, **Rob Nelson**, head of development and co-studio head at Rockstar North, described the small systems that make Jason and Lucia's routine feel lived-in. The common thread is realism: objects exist physically in the world, the couple's home behaves like a real home, and the open world respects the needs of the story. Check out the main highlights of the new details: - **A phone you actually hold:** The cell phone is now a physical object in Jason and Lucia's hands instead of a flat 2D overlay, as it was in GTA V. Rockstar mentioned apps for video, fitness tracking, banking, social media and "Scooter Bros", a vehicle delivery service. - **Photos, but no posting:** Jason and Lucia can send photos to each other. Because both are on the run, though, they cannot upload anything to social media; they can only follow other accounts. - **A home that feels shared:** The hideout is treated as a place where two people live. In the demo shown to Famitsu, Jason pulls back the covers and climbs into bed next to a sleeping Lucia. You also can't toss objects anywhere: Nelson explained that a mug has to be carried to a place where it can properly be put down. - **Protected story locations:** As in Red Dead Redemption 2, some places that matter to the story are off-limits for crime. Nelson's example: you can't steal cars outside the strip club owned by Jason's friend Dre'Quan, so players can't accidentally ruin a location the story still needs. - **A body to look after:** How you play changes Jason and Lucia's bodies. Training builds muscle, overeating can make them gain weight, and food gives temporary boosts to their health and stamina meters. Together, these details point to a slower, more grounded GTA, closer to the daily rhythm of Red Dead Redemption 2 than to the arcade feel of earlier games. For everything confirmed about money, gyms and hideouts, read our guide: [GTA 6 gameplay: money, gym and hideouts](https://vvviceversa.com/guides/gta-6-gameplay-money-gym-hideouts/). GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges!

context: The Famitsu interview, conducted at Rockstar North in Edinburgh and published in English by GTAVice on September 9, is one of several long conversations Rob Nelson gave around the late-August Extended Look. In Dazed, he said food would affect Jason and Lucia's weight, workouts would build visible muscle and lack of sleep would show in their faces. In IGN's interview, later republished in full, he said the couple can only browse the Snapmatic social app because they are fugitives, and compared GTA VI's safehouses to the camps in Red Dead Redemption 2.
Read together, the interviews describe one design direction from different angles: more physical interaction, fewer abstract menus and a world that keeps track of what you do.
known: Nelson told Famitsu the phone is now a physical object in the world rather than GTA V's 2D overlay, with video, fitness and banking apps and a car delivery service called Scooter Bros.
Jason and Lucia can send each other photos but cannot post on social media; in IGN's interview Nelson summed it up as "You just lurk."
Car theft is blocked around hideouts and at some story locations, such as outside the strip club owned by Jason's friend Dre'Quan.
Workouts build muscle and overeating leads to weight gain, a point Nelson made to Famitsu, Dazed and IGN.
Food and drink give temporary boosts, such as an energy drink raising stamina, while training raises base health and stamina.
unknown: How much body changes affect gameplay beyond health and stamina has not been detailed.
Rockstar has not listed the protected locations or explained how the game tells players where crime is restricted.
The full list of phone apps, and whether new ones unlock during the story, is unknown.
take: These details matter more than they look. A phone that exists in the hand, a mug that needs a surface, cars you cannot steal outside a friend's club: each is a small rule that trades convenience for coherence. Red Dead Redemption 2 was built on the same trade, and Nelson's comparison of safehouses to its camps suggests Rockstar is comfortable carrying that philosophy into a series known for chaos.

The protected-locations rule is the most practical of them. It solves a real problem, players wrecking a place the story still needs, by restricting freedom in a narrow way instead of breaking a mission later. The risk is in the signalling: an unexplained no-theft zone around a strip club could feel arbitrary. The body system is the other one to watch. San Andreas tied fitness to play back in 2004, and GTA VI now has to show that eating and training matter beyond what players see in the mirror.

context: A entrevista à Famitsu, feita na Rockstar North, em Edimburgo, e publicada em inglês pela GTAVice em 9 de setembro, é uma de várias conversas longas que Rob Nelson deu em torno do Extended Look, no fim de agosto. À Dazed, ele disse que a comida afeta o peso de Jason e Lucia, que malhar gera músculos visíveis e que noites sem dormir aparecem no rosto. Na entrevista à IGN, depois republicada na íntegra, contou que o casal só pode navegar no app Snapmatic por ser fugitivo e comparou os esconderijos aos acampamentos de Red Dead Redemption 2.
Lidas juntas, as entrevistas descrevem a mesma direção por ângulos diferentes: mais interação física, menos menus abstratos e um mundo que registra o que você faz.

Jason e Lucia podem trocar fotos, mas não podem postar em redes sociais; na entrevista à IGN, Nelson resumiu: “You just lurk” (“Você só observa”).
Roubar carros é bloqueado em volta dos esconderijos e em alguns locais da história, como na frente da boate de strip do amigo de Jason, Dre'Quan.
Malhar gera músculos e comer demais faz engordar, algo que Nelson repetiu à Famitsu, à Dazed e à IGN.
Comida e bebida dão bônus temporários, como um energético que aumenta o fôlego, enquanto o treino eleva a vida e o fôlego de base.

A Rockstar não listou os locais protegidos nem explicou como o jogo avisa onde o crime é restrito.
A lista completa de apps do celular, e se novos são liberados ao longo da história, é desconhecida.
take: Esses detalhes pesam mais do que parecem. Um celular que existe na mão, uma caneca que precisa de uma superfície, carros que não dá para roubar na porta da boate de um amigo: cada um é uma pequena regra que troca conveniência por coerência. Red Dead Redemption 2 foi construído sobre essa mesma troca, e a comparação de Nelson entre os esconderijos e os acampamentos indica que a Rockstar está à vontade para levar essa filosofia a uma série famosa pelo caos.

A regra dos locais protegidos é a mais prática delas. Resolve um problema real, o jogador destruir um lugar de que a história ainda precisa, limitando a liberdade de forma pontual em vez de quebrar uma missão depois. O risco está na sinalização: uma zona sem roubo de carro na frente de uma boate, sem explicação, pode parecer arbitrária. O sistema de corpo é o outro ponto de atenção. San Andreas já ligava forma física ao gameplay em 2004, e GTA VI agora precisa mostrar que comer e treinar importam além do espelho.

titulo_es: Así es la vida diaria en GTA 6: móvil físico, escondite compartido y lugares protegidos de la historia
texto_es: A 65 días del lanzamiento, Rockstar sigue revelando cómo será la vida en Leonida entre misión y misión. En una larga entrevista con la revista japonesa **Famitsu**, traducida al inglés por GTAVice, **Rob Nelson**, jefe de desarrollo y codirector de Rockstar North, describió los pequeños sistemas que dan vida a la rutina de Jason y Lucia. El hilo conductor es el realismo: los objetos existen de verdad en el mundo, la casa de la pareja funciona como una casa real y el mundo abierto respeta las necesidades de la historia. Estos son los puntos más destacados: - **Un móvil que de verdad sostienes:** El teléfono es ahora un objeto físico en las manos de Jason y Lucia, y no una capa 2D sobre la pantalla como en GTA V. Rockstar mencionó aplicaciones de vídeo, seguimiento de ejercicio, banca, redes sociales y "Scooter Bros", un servicio de entrega de vehículos. - **Fotos, pero sin publicar:** Jason y Lucia pueden enviarse fotos. Como los dos están huyendo, no pueden publicar nada en redes sociales; solo pueden seguir otras cuentas. - **Un hogar compartido:** El escondite se trata como el lugar donde viven dos personas. En la demostración mostrada a Famitsu, Jason aparta las sábanas y se mete en la cama junto a Lucia, que duerme. Tampoco se pueden tirar objetos en cualquier sitio: según Nelson, una taza hay que llevarla a un lugar donde se pueda dejar como es debido. - **Lugares protegidos de la historia:** Como en Red Dead Redemption 2, algunos lugares importantes para la historia no permiten delitos. El ejemplo de Nelson: no se pueden robar coches a la puerta del club de striptease de Dre'Quan, amigo de Jason, para que el jugador no estropee sin querer un sitio que la historia aún necesita. - **Un cuerpo que cuidar:** La forma de jugar cambia el cuerpo de Jason y Lucia. Entrenar gana músculo, comer de más puede hacer engordar y la comida da mejoras temporales a los indicadores de salud y resistencia. En conjunto, estos detalles apuntan a un GTA más pausado y realista, más cerca del ritmo diario de Red Dead Redemption 2 que del estilo arcade de las entregas anteriores. Todo lo confirmado sobre dinero, gimnasio y escondites está en nuestra guía: [jugabilidad de GTA 6: dinero, gimnasio y escondites](https://vvviceversa.com/es/guias/jugabilidad-gta-6-dinero-gimnasio-escondites/). titulo: Miami Beach Votes to Negotiate GTA 6 Marketing Deal: 'Vice City' Beach Ads Proposed From October 15
texto: Vice City is about to take over the real Miami Beach. On September 10, 2026, the **Miami Beach City Commission** voted 4–3 to authorize negotiations on a marketing deal that would bring Grand Theft Auto VI branding to the city's beaches ahead of the game's launch. As of October 12, the contract had still not been signed, according to reporter Joel Franco via GTA BOOM. The approval came after a heated debate. Commissioner David Suarez opposed the deal, showed footage from the game during the session and said he did not want the city's brand associated with it. Separately, Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz had criticized a different GTA 6 promotion proposed to Miami-Dade County, pointing to the series' focus on crime. Supporters, like Commissioner Monica Matteo-Salinas, argued that enjoying fiction is not the same as endorsing crime, and stressed the financial benefit for the city. Check out the main proposed terms of the campaign: - **Where the ads will appear:** Only on private beach equipment, the chairs and umbrellas run by the concessionaire Boucher Brothers. No Rockstar branding will go on city property such as lifeguard stands. - **What they will show:** The ads are limited to the Roman numeral "VI" and the name "Vice City", described as discreet placements. - **When:** The proposal calls for **October 15 to December 31, 2026**, covering the November 19 launch and the holiday season, but with the contract still unsigned, the start date will likely slip. - **How much:** Reports put the value of the deal in the millions of dollars, with Beebom citing about $3 million. The campaign is not limited to the beach. On September 14, a photo shared on Reddit showed large advertising panels laid out behind the Kaseya Center, the Miami Heat's arena in downtown Miami, which turned out to form a "Welcome to Vice City" sign. It was installed on the arena's roof on September 22 as part of a separate $975,000 deal with Miami-Dade County. Miami is the real-world inspiration for Vice City, and Rockstar seems ready to make the most of it. If you are in Florida this fall, expect to see the city and the game blend together. To learn how Vice City fits into the state of Leonida, read our guide: [the GTA 6 map and Leonida's regions](https://vvviceversa.com/guides/gta-6-map-leonida-regions/). Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges! *Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article said Miami Beach approved the deal, that the sheriff criticized it and that the Kaseya Center sign would read "Welcome to VI." In fact, the 4–3 vote only authorized negotiations, the contract was still unsigned as of October 12, the sheriff criticized a separate Miami-Dade County proposal, and the sign reads "Welcome to Vice City."*

context: The Miami Beach vote is part of a wider push to turn the real Miami into a billboard for Vice City before the November 19 launch. In early September, the Miami Herald reported that Miami-Dade County had discussed ideas such as “Welcome to Vice City” messages at Miami International Airport and branded Metromover cars, which led Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz to object in public. The county also approved, without a commission vote, a $975,000 “Welcome to Vice City” sign on the roof of the Kaseya Center, which went up in September.

What Miami Beach approved on September 10 was the authority to negotiate, not a signed contract. Commissioners discussed a fee of about $3 million, and one suggested it could get closer to $4 million.
known: On September 10, 2026, the Miami Beach City Commission voted 4–3 to open negotiations on a GTA VI marketing campaign.
The planned branding is limited to “VI” and “Vice City” on beach chairs and umbrellas run by the concessionaire Boucher Brothers, not on city buildings.
The campaign window discussed runs from October 15 to the end of 2026, covering the November 19 launch.
In October, county commissioners postponed a broader proposal covering the airport, PortMiami and transit, and required any Rockstar deal above $1 million to come back to them.
unknown: As of October 12, a report citing a city official said the Miami Beach contract had not been signed, so the October 15 start may slip.
The final fee Miami Beach will receive has not been made public.
Whether any county property, such as Miami International Airport, will carry GTA VI branding remains open; Mayor Daniella Levine Cava says talks continue.
take: The beach chairs are the least interesting part of this story. The real question is how closely Rockstar can tie GTA VI to a real city, and how much pushback it gets. So far the pattern is clear: local governments like the money but get nervous once the branding moves onto public property. Miami Beach confined it to a private concessionaire's umbrellas, and the county approved a sign priced just under the threshold that would have required a vote, then stalled on the airport and transit ideas.

For readers, the practical point is that the September vote was a first step, not a finished deal. Early coverage, ours included, presented October 15 as a fixed start date, and that now looks uncertain. Two things are worth watching before launch: whether Miami Beach signs in time to matter, and whether the county proposal returns to the agenda. Discreet “VI” logos can survive a short delay. A campaign timed to a release date cannot wait much longer.

texto: In an interview with the Japanese magazine **Famitsu**, **Rob Nelson**, head of development and co-studio head at Rockstar North, gave one of the most detailed explanations yet of how Grand Theft Auto VI plays. He covered how Jason and Lucia's relationship works, the return of gyms and a police system rebuilt from scratch. Here are the highlights, organized by topic. ### Jason and Lucia: characters and relationship Rockstar first considered **four playable characters**, but settled on two. According to Nelson, the team learned with Arthur Morgan in Red Dead Redemption 2 that fewer protagonists means more screen time for each one and a stronger emotional bond with the player. - **Partners in crime or a couple:** Players choose how to treat the relationship. Skipping the romance closes off some interactions, such as holding hands or kissing, but the main story can be completed either way. - **Switching characters:** You can switch freely between Jason and Lucia in the open world, except at specific story moments. In one specific early mission, set in a high-rise housing complex, control is locked to Jason. - **Hideouts that change:** As with the camp in RDR2, the story is told in chapters, and the couple's hideout changes as it progresses. ### Gyms are back - **Body stats:** The game tracks each character's health, stamina and fitness. Depending on your habits, they can gain muscle or body fat. - **Workouts:** Gym minigames return, as in GTA San Andreas. Leveling up takes consistency: Rockstar described a routine of three exercises a day for three days in a row. - **Food:** Eating gives temporary boosts to health and stamina on top of the base values you raise by training. ### A smarter wanted system - **Witnesses:** As in RDR2, a crime only reaches the police if someone sees it and reports it. - **Cash vs. bank:** Money now works like GTA Online. Cash you carry is lost if you die or get arrested; money deposited in the bank is safe. - **Criminal profile:** The game evaluates what kind of criminal you are, for example a professional one or a violent and dangerous one. - **No more invisible rifles:** Long guns are now visible on your character and must be stored at Ammu-Nation or in a car trunk to stay discreet. Taken together, the interview shows a GTA built around consequences: what you eat, where you keep your money and who sees you all matter. For the full breakdown of the police system, read our guide: [the GTA 6 wanted system](https://vvviceversa.com/guides/gta-6-wanted-system-police/). GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges! *Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article said control is locked to Jason at the very start of the game and that the criminal profile can push you into a "chaotic state." In fact, the lock applies to one specific early mission, and the criminal profile evaluates what kind of criminal you are, such as professional or violent.*

context: Rob Nelson's Famitsu interview, translated into English by GTAVice on September 9, was one of several conversations he gave after Rockstar's August 27 Extended Look on Netflix. He had already spoken at length to IGN, which later published the full transcript, and to Dazed. Read together, the interviews describe a GTA that borrows heavily from Red Dead Redemption 2: safehouses compared to Arthur Morgan's camps, a relationship system between Jason and Lucia, and police who only react to what witnesses actually see.
The Famitsu conversation went further on some systems, such as the gym routine, cash lost on death or arrest, and long guns that can no longer be carried invisibly.
known: Rockstar considered four protagonists before settling on two, to give players more time with each character, Nelson told IGN.
The romance between Jason and Lucia is optional, and the story keeps them working together as partners for most of the game either way.
Crimes are reported only when a witness sees them or an alarm goes off, and changing outfits helps shake off the police.
Diet and exercise change the characters' body shape, and gyms let players build strength.
A Criminal Profile tracks behavior that goes beyond what missions require; it is separate from the relationship system and different from RDR2's honor system.
unknown: The gym routine described in the Famitsu translation, three exercises a day over three days, has not been shown in footage.
How much the relationship changes the story: Nelson said it will “have a bearing” on how it plays out, without giving specifics.
How banking and cash loss are balanced in single player is known only from Famitsu's description, not from gameplay.
take: The common thread across Nelson's interviews is friction. Cars that need tools to steal, cash you can lose, rifles you have to stash, outfits the police remember: each system asks you to plan instead of improvise. That is a deliberate step away from GTA V, where the world mostly reacted to the player, and toward Red Dead Redemption 2, where it pushed back. RDR2 showed this approach can deepen immersion. It also showed it can slow a game down.

Some caution with the details is still warranted. The Famitsu text reached English through a fan translation, and a few points have been stretched in retellings, our own summary included: the lock on Jason applies to one early mission, not the whole opening. The elements Nelson repeated to several outlets, the optional romance, witness-based policing and the criminal profile, are the ones to treat as settled. Everything else will be tested on November 19.

context: A entrevista de Rob Nelson à Famitsu, traduzida para o inglês pelo GTAVice em 9 de setembro, foi uma de várias conversas que ele deu depois do Extended Look da Rockstar na Netflix, em 27 de agosto. Ele já tinha falado longamente ao IGN, que depois publicou a transcrição completa, e à Dazed. Lidas em conjunto, as entrevistas descrevem um GTA que pega muito de Red Dead Redemption 2: esconderijos comparados aos acampamentos de Arthur Morgan, um sistema de relacionamento entre Jason e Lucia e uma polícia que só reage ao que as testemunhas realmente veem.

A conversa com a Famitsu foi mais a fundo em alguns sistemas, como a rotina de academia, a perda do dinheiro vivo ao morrer ou ser preso e as armas longas que deixam de ser carregadas de forma invisível.
known: A Rockstar chegou a considerar quatro protagonistas antes de ficar com dois, para dar mais tempo ao jogador com cada personagem, segundo Nelson ao IGN.
O romance entre Jason e Lucia é opcional, e a história mantém os dois trabalhando juntos como parceiros durante a maior parte do jogo de qualquer forma.
Os crimes só são denunciados quando uma testemunha vê ou quando um alarme dispara, e trocar de roupa ajuda a despistar a polícia.
Alimentação e exercício mudam o corpo dos personagens, e as academias permitem ganhar força.
Um Criminal Profile registra o comportamento que vai além do que as missões exigem; ele é separado do relacionamento e diferente do sistema de honra de RDR2.
unknown: A rotina de academia descrita na tradução da Famitsu, com três exercícios por dia durante três dias, ainda não apareceu em vídeo.
Quanto o relacionamento muda a história: Nelson disse que ele terá “influência” no desenrolar da trama, sem dar detalhes.
Como o banco e a perda de dinheiro vivo funcionam na prática no modo história só é conhecido pela descrição da Famitsu, não por gameplay.
take: O que une as entrevistas de Nelson é o atrito. Carros que exigem ferramentas para roubar, dinheiro que pode ser perdido, fuzis que precisam ser guardados, roupas que a polícia memoriza: cada sistema pede planejamento em vez de improviso. É um afastamento deliberado de GTA V, em que o mundo basicamente reagia ao jogador, rumo a Red Dead Redemption 2, em que o mundo resistia. RDR2 mostrou que essa abordagem pode aprofundar a imersão. Também mostrou que pode deixar o ritmo mais lento.

Ainda assim, vale cautela com os detalhes. O texto da Famitsu chegou ao inglês por uma tradução de fã, e alguns pontos foram esticados nas releituras, inclusive no nosso resumo: o bloqueio no Jason vale para uma missão do início, não para toda a abertura. Os elementos que Nelson repetiu a vários veículos, o romance opcional, a polícia baseada em testemunhas e o perfil criminal, são os que podem ser tratados como certos. O resto será posto à prova em 19 de novembro.

In an interview with the Japanese magazine Famitsu, Rob Nelson, head of development and co-studio head at Rockstar North, gave one of the most detailed explanations yet of how Grand Theft Auto VI plays. He covered how Jason and Lucia's relationship works, the return of gyms and a police system rebuilt from scratch. Here are the highlights, organized by topic.

Jason and Lucia: characters and relationship

Rockstar first considered four playable characters, but settled on two. According to Nelson, the team learned with Arthur Morgan in Red Dead Redemption 2 that fewer protagonists means more screen time for each one and a stronger emotional bond with the player.

  • Partners in crime or a couple: Players choose how to treat the relationship. Skipping the romance closes off some interactions, such as holding hands or kissing, but the main story can be completed either way.
  • Switching characters: You can switch freely between Jason and Lucia in the open world, except at specific story moments. In one specific early mission, set in a high-rise housing complex, control is locked to Jason.
  • Hideouts that change: As with the camp in RDR2, the story is told in chapters, and the couple's hideout changes as it progresses.

Gyms are back

  • Body stats: The game tracks each character's health, stamina and fitness. Depending on your habits, they can gain muscle or body fat.
  • Workouts: Gym minigames return, as in GTA San Andreas. Leveling up takes consistency: Rockstar described a routine of three exercises a day for three days in a row.
  • Food: Eating gives temporary boosts to health and stamina on top of the base values you raise by training.

A smarter wanted system

  • Witnesses: As in RDR2, a crime only reaches the police if someone sees it and reports it.
  • Cash vs. bank: Money now works like GTA Online. Cash you carry is lost if you die or get arrested; money deposited in the bank is safe.
  • Criminal profile: The game evaluates what kind of criminal you are, for example a professional one or a violent and dangerous one.
  • No more invisible rifles: Long guns are now visible on your character and must be stored at Ammu-Nation or in a car trunk to stay discreet.

Taken together, the interview shows a GTA built around consequences: what you eat, where you keep your money and who sees you all matter. For the full breakdown of the police system, read our guide: the GTA 6 wanted system.

GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

titulo_pt: Rockstar explica os dois protagonistas, as academias e o novo sistema de procurado de GTA 6 à Famitsu
texto_pt: Em entrevista à revista japonesa **Famitsu**, **Rob Nelson**, chefe de desenvolvimento e codiretor da Rockstar North, deu uma das explicações mais detalhadas até agora sobre como se joga Grand Theft Auto VI. Ele falou sobre como funciona a relação entre Jason e Lucia, a volta das academias e um sistema de polícia refeito do zero. Veja os destaques, organizados por tema. ### Jason e Lucia: personagens e relacionamento A Rockstar chegou a pensar em **quatro personagens jogáveis**, mas ficou com dois. Segundo Nelson, a equipe aprendeu com Arthur Morgan, em Red Dead Redemption 2, que menos protagonistas significam mais tempo de tela para cada um e um vínculo emocional mais forte com o jogador. - **Parceiros no crime ou casal:** O jogador escolhe como tratar a relação. Recusar o romance fecha algumas interações, como andar de mãos dadas ou beijar, mas a história principal pode ser concluída dos dois jeitos. - **Troca de personagem:** Dá para alternar livremente entre Jason e Lucia no mundo aberto, exceto em momentos específicos da história. Em uma missão específica do início do jogo, num conjunto habitacional de prédios altos, o controle fica preso em Jason. - **Esconderijos que mudam:** Como o acampamento de RDR2, a história é contada em capítulos, e o esconderijo do casal muda conforme ela avança. ### As academias estão de volta - **Atributos do corpo:** O jogo acompanha a vida, o fôlego e o condicionamento de cada personagem. Dependendo dos hábitos do jogador, eles podem ganhar músculos ou gordura. - **Treinos:** Os minigames de academia voltam, como em GTA San Andreas. Evoluir exige constância: a Rockstar descreveu uma rotina de três exercícios por dia, durante três dias seguidos. - **Comida:** Comer dá bônus temporários de vida e fôlego acima dos valores básicos, que sobem com o treino. ### Um sistema de procurado mais inteligente - **Testemunhas:** Como em RDR2, um crime só chega à polícia se alguém vir e denunciar. - **Carteira x banco:** O dinheiro agora funciona como em GTA Online. O dinheiro vivo que você carrega é perdido se morrer ou for preso; o que está depositado no banco fica seguro. - **Perfil criminal:** O jogo avalia que tipo de criminoso você é, por exemplo, um criminoso profissional ou um violento e perigoso. - **Fim dos fuzis invisíveis:** Armas longas agora aparecem no corpo do personagem e precisam ser guardadas na Ammu-Nation ou no porta-malas de um carro para passar despercebidas. No conjunto, a entrevista mostra um GTA construído em torno de consequências: o que você come, onde guarda o dinheiro e quem te vê, tudo importa. Para a explicação completa do sistema de polícia, leia nosso guia: [o sistema de procurado de GTA 6](https://vvviceversa.com/pt/guias/sistema-procurado-policia-gta-6/). GTA VI chega em 19 de novembro de 2026 para PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S. Fique ligado no nosso site para mais atualizações e a cobertura completa assim que surgirem novas informações sobre GTA 6! *Correção (16 de outubro de 2026): uma versão anterior deste artigo dizia que o controle fica preso em Jason no começo do jogo e que o perfil criminal pode levar a um "estado caótico". Na verdade, a trava vale para uma missão específica do início do jogo, e o perfil criminal avalia que tipo de criminoso você é, como profissional ou violento.*

Em entrevista à revista japonesa Famitsu, Rob Nelson, chefe de desenvolvimento e codiretor da Rockstar North, deu uma das explicações mais detalhadas até agora sobre como se joga Grand Theft Auto VI. Ele falou sobre como funciona a relação entre Jason e Lucia, a volta das academias e um sistema de polícia refeito do zero. Veja os destaques, organizados por tema.

Jason e Lucia: personagens e relacionamento

A Rockstar chegou a pensar em quatro personagens jogáveis, mas ficou com dois. Segundo Nelson, a equipe aprendeu com Arthur Morgan, em Red Dead Redemption 2, que menos protagonistas significam mais tempo de tela para cada um e um vínculo emocional mais forte com o jogador.

  • Parceiros no crime ou casal: O jogador escolhe como tratar a relação. Recusar o romance fecha algumas interações, como andar de mãos dadas ou beijar, mas a história principal pode ser concluída dos dois jeitos.
  • Troca de personagem: Dá para alternar livremente entre Jason e Lucia no mundo aberto, exceto em momentos específicos da história. Em uma missão específica do início do jogo, num conjunto habitacional de prédios altos, o controle fica preso em Jason.
  • Esconderijos que mudam: Como o acampamento de RDR2, a história é contada em capítulos, e o esconderijo do casal muda conforme ela avança.

As academias estão de volta

  • Atributos do corpo: O jogo acompanha a vida, o fôlego e o condicionamento de cada personagem. Dependendo dos hábitos do jogador, eles podem ganhar músculos ou gordura.
  • Treinos: Os minigames de academia voltam, como em GTA San Andreas. Evoluir exige constância: a Rockstar descreveu uma rotina de três exercícios por dia, durante três dias seguidos.
  • Comida: Comer dá bônus temporários de vida e fôlego acima dos valores básicos, que sobem com o treino.

Um sistema de procurado mais inteligente

  • Testemunhas: Como em RDR2, um crime só chega à polícia se alguém vir e denunciar.
  • Carteira x banco: O dinheiro agora funciona como em GTA Online. O dinheiro vivo que você carrega é perdido se morrer ou for preso; o que está depositado no banco fica seguro.
  • Perfil criminal: O jogo avalia que tipo de criminoso você é, por exemplo, um criminoso profissional ou um violento e perigoso.
  • Fim dos fuzis invisíveis: Armas longas agora aparecem no corpo do personagem e precisam ser guardadas na Ammu-Nation ou no porta-malas de um carro para passar despercebidas.

No conjunto, a entrevista mostra um GTA construído em torno de consequências: o que você come, onde guarda o dinheiro e quem te vê, tudo importa. Para a explicação completa do sistema de polícia, leia nosso guia: o sistema de procurado de GTA 6.

GTA VI chega em 19 de novembro de 2026 para PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S.

Fique ligado no nosso site para mais atualizações e a cobertura completa assim que surgirem novas informações sobre GTA 6!

Correção (16 de outubro de 2026): uma versão anterior deste artigo dizia que o controle fica preso em Jason no começo do jogo e que o perfil criminal pode levar a um "estado caótico". Na verdade, a trava vale para uma missão específica do início do jogo, e o perfil criminal avalia que tipo de criminoso você é, como profissional ou violento.
titulo_es: Rockstar explica a Famitsu los dos protagonistas, los gimnasios y el nuevo sistema de búsqueda de GTA 6
texto_es: En una entrevista con la revista japonesa **Famitsu**, **Rob Nelson**, jefe de desarrollo y codirector de Rockstar North, dio una de las explicaciones más detalladas hasta ahora sobre cómo se juega a Grand Theft Auto VI. Habló de cómo funciona la relación entre Jason y Lucia, de la vuelta de los gimnasios y de un sistema policial rehecho desde cero. Estos son los puntos clave, por temas. ### Jason y Lucia: personajes y relación Rockstar llegó a plantearse **cuatro personajes jugables**, pero se quedó con dos. Según Nelson, el equipo aprendió con Arthur Morgan en Red Dead Redemption 2 que menos protagonistas significan más tiempo en pantalla para cada uno y un vínculo emocional más fuerte con el jugador. - **Cómplices o pareja:** El jugador elige cómo tratar la relación. Rechazar el romance cierra algunas interacciones, como ir de la mano o besarse, pero la historia principal se puede completar de las dos formas. - **Cambio de personaje:** Se puede cambiar libremente entre Jason y Lucia en el mundo abierto, salvo en momentos concretos de la historia. En una misión concreta del inicio del juego, en un complejo de viviendas de edificios altos, el control está fijado en Jason. - **Escondites que cambian:** Como el campamento de RDR2, la historia se cuenta por capítulos y el escondite de la pareja cambia a medida que avanza. ### Vuelven los gimnasios - **Atributos físicos:** El juego registra la salud, la resistencia y la forma física de cada personaje. Según tus hábitos, pueden ganar músculo o grasa. - **Entrenamientos:** Los minijuegos de gimnasio regresan, como en GTA San Andreas. Mejorar exige constancia: Rockstar describió una rutina de tres ejercicios al día durante tres días seguidos. - **Comida:** Comer da mejoras temporales de salud y resistencia por encima de los valores base, que se suben entrenando. ### Un sistema de búsqueda más inteligente - **Testigos:** Como en RDR2, un delito solo llega a la policía si alguien lo ve y lo denuncia. - **Efectivo y banco:** El dinero funciona ahora como en GTA Online. El efectivo que llevas se pierde si mueres o te detienen; lo depositado en el banco está a salvo. - **Perfil criminal:** El juego evalúa qué tipo de criminal eres, por ejemplo, uno profesional o uno violento y peligroso. - **Adiós a los rifles invisibles:** Las armas largas ahora se ven en el personaje y hay que guardarlas en Ammu-Nation o en el maletero de un coche para pasar desapercibido. En conjunto, la entrevista muestra un GTA construido en torno a las consecuencias: lo que comes, dónde guardas el dinero y quién te ve, todo cuenta. Para la explicación completa del sistema policial, lee nuestra guía: [el sistema de búsqueda de GTA 6](https://vvviceversa.com/es/guias/sistema-busqueda-policia-gta-6/). GTA VI llega el 19 de noviembre de 2026 a PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S. ¡Sigue atento a nuestra web para más novedades y la cobertura completa en cuanto surja nueva información sobre GTA 6! *Corrección (16 de octubre de 2026): una versión anterior de este artículo decía que el control está fijado en Jason al principio del juego y que el perfil criminal puede llevarte a un "estado caótico". En realidad, el bloqueo se aplica a una misión concreta del inicio del juego, y el perfil criminal evalúa qué tipo de criminal eres, como profesional o violento.*

GTA VI llega el 19 de noviembre de 2026 a PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S.

titulo: GTA 6 Limited-Edition DualSense Controllers Open for Pre-Order at $84.99
texto: Pre-orders for the **Grand Theft Auto VI limited-edition DualSense controllers** opened on September 10, 2026, at 7:00 a.m. PT (10:00 a.m. ET) in the United States and at 10:00 a.m. local time in the UK and Europe. Sony first revealed the two designs during the PlayStation State of Play on September 3. Each controller costs **$84.99** (¥12,480 in Japan) and ships on **November 19, 2026**, the same day the game launches on PlayStation 5. Check out the main details of each version: - **White Limited Edition:** Pastel tones inspired by "Vice City at daybreak", with a sun-bleached beach look. It is sold on PlayStation Direct and at participating retailers worldwide. - **Black Limited Edition:** A black body with shimmering neon-purple gradients that evoke Vice City at night. In the US, the UK and several European countries, including Spain, France, Germany and Italy, it is **exclusive to PlayStation Direct**. - **Shared details:** Both feature palm tree shapes on the grips, the GTA VI logo on the touchpad, purple face buttons and D-pad, and the Rockstar logo on the back. - **Same hardware:** Inside, they are standard DualSense controllers. There are no performance upgrades and nothing is unlocked in the game; the price reflects the cosmetic design only. Themed controllers tend to sell out quickly, and the black version, available only on Sony's store in many countries, is the one most likely to disappear first. If you want one for launch day, pre-ordering is the safest bet; you can find the US listing for the black edition on PlayStation Direct, linked in the sources below. Planning your launch-day purchase? See every edition of the game and its price in our guide: [GTA 6 editions, prices and pre-orders](https://vvviceversa.com/guides/gta-6-editions-prices-pre-order/). Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges!

context: Sony revealed the two controllers at its September 3 State of Play, with GTA VI due on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Custom DualSense pads for big third-party games are not new, but they are usually a single design; GTA VI gets two, one for Vice City by day and one for its nightlife.

Price is part of the story. At $84.99, each pad costs $15 more than a standard DualSense, which lists at $69.99, for no change in hardware. The controllers ship on November 19, the same day as the game, and Sony sold them in limited quantities from the start.
known: Pre-orders opened September 10 at 7:00 a.m. PT in the US and 10:00 a.m. local time in the UK and several European countries.
Both editions cost $84.99, £74.99, €84.99 or ¥12,480, and ship on November 19.
PlayStation Direct struggled on launch morning, with hour-long queues and checkout errors reported by Kotaku.
In the US, Best Buy, Walmart and GameStop sold only the white edition, while the black edition stayed on Sony's own store.
Sony limited purchases to one per customer, and eBay listings asking $130 to $195 appeared the same day.
unknown: Sony has not said how many units were made or whether more stock will be released before launch.
Whether pre-ordered controllers will arrive on November 19 or a day or two earlier is not confirmed.
Microsoft has not announced a GTA VI-themed Xbox controller.
take: Our original piece urged readers to hurry, and that advice aged within hours: the white edition sold out at Best Buy and several UK stores on the first day, while PlayStation Direct buckled under hour-long queues. That says less about the controllers than about the mood around GTA VI. A purely cosmetic accessory, with the same internals as a standard DualSense, sold like a limited sneaker drop, and resellers moved in before a single unit had shipped.

If you missed out, paying $150 or more on eBay for an $85 controller is hard to justify. The pad does nothing a regular DualSense cannot, and resale prices for preorders depend on sellers actually receiving stock. The more useful signal is what this demand means for November 19. If a controller can overwhelm PlayStation Direct, it is reasonable to expect similar pressure on console stock as launch gets closer, so anyone who still needs hardware should plan earlier rather than later.

titulo: GTA 6's New HUD Makes Losing the Cops Harder: No More Police Dots on the Minimap
texto: The GTA 6 **Extended Look**, shown on Netflix in August 2026, made one thing clear: Rockstar has completely redesigned the game's HUD, and the change hits hardest where veterans feel it most — escaping the police. For years, the trick in Grand Theft Auto was simple: watch the minimap, avoid the red dots and their vision cones, and wait for the stars to fade. In GTA 6, that safety net is gone. Check out the main changes to the wanted system's HUD: - **No more "all-seeing" minimap:** The classic red dots showing each officer's exact position and line of sight have disappeared. Instead, a flashing red-and-blue zone marks the general area where the police are searching for you. Rockstar calls this state **Heat**. - **Hanger icon — your clothes:** Shows that the police know what you are wearing. Changing outfits becomes a real way to throw them off. - **Face icon — your identity:** Shows whether a witness or a security camera has identified you, or whether a mask kept your face hidden. - **Vehicle icon — your getaway car:** Lets you know if the cops or cameras have identified the car you are using. - **Partner icon — your accomplice:** Shows whether the police know you had someone with you during the crime, which matters in a game built around Jason and Lucia working as a pair. In practice, the HUD now tells you what the police **know**, not where they **are**. To find officers, you have to look around, use cover and blend into traffic. Rockstar's Rob Nelson later added in an interview with Famitsu that crimes depend on witnesses, while the Extended Look, shown on August 27, revealed a wanted meter with room for six stars. It is a big shift for a series that made fleeing the cops almost routine. Expect getaways to take more planning: masks, a change of clothes and a backup car may be as important as a fast engine. For tips on how to lose the police based on everything Rockstar has shown, read our guide: [the GTA 6 wanted system](https://vvviceversa.com/guides/gta-6-wanted-system-police/). GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges! *Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article said Rob Nelson mentioned a six-star wanted scale in his Famitsu interview. In fact, the six stars were shown in the Extended Look on August 27; the Famitsu interview covered the role of witnesses.*

context: In GTA V, police showed up on the radar with vision cones, so escaping was mostly a matter of staying out of their sight lines. The Extended Look, which premiered on Netflix on August 27, showed that GTA VI drops that model. During a four-star chase, the minimap displayed a red search area instead of individual officers, and players now spot nearby police with Focus, a new ability that highlights useful details in the world.
The change comes with a sixth wanted star, absent from GTA V, and a description system that records what police know about the player's outfit, appearance, car and accomplice.
known: Police no longer appear as individual dots on the minimap; a search area marks where they are looking.
Icons under the wanted stars show what police know, such as your outfit, appearance, vehicle and whether you had an accomplice; a hollow star means they know a crime happened but not who did it.
Crimes are reported only if a witness sees them or an alarm goes off.
A full outfit change helps shed a description; sunglasses or a hat do not, and a mask during a job can keep your face unknown.
The wanted level goes up to six stars, one more than GTA V.
unknown: A preview mentioned HUD options, including a classic minimap mode, but Rockstar has not said whether any setting shows individual officers again.
How long police keep a description on record, and how the CCTV indicator works in practice, has not been detailed.
Rockstar has not explained what triggers six stars or how police behave at that level.
take: This is the most consequential design change Rockstar has shown so far, because it touches the loop players repeat most often. In GTA V, a chase ended once you slipped out of the cones on the radar. In GTA VI, the HUD reports what the police know rather than where they are, which moves the work from reflexes to preparation: a mask before the job, a spare outfit in the car, a second vehicle parked nearby.

The risk is that friction turns into tedium in a series that also sells itself on chaos. Rockstar appears to be aware of it. Nelson has said that actions taken during missions do not count against the criminal profile, and Focus gives players a way to find officers without the radar doing it for them. Whether that balance holds over 80 hours of play is the real test, and it cannot be judged from a curated showcase. The direction, at least, is coherent.

context: Em GTA V, a polícia aparecia no radar com cones de visão, e fugir era basicamente questão de ficar fora do campo de vista dos policiais. O Extended Look, exibido na Netflix em 27 de agosto, mostrou que GTA VI abandona esse modelo. Durante uma perseguição de quatro estrelas, o minimapa exibia uma área de busca vermelha em vez dos policiais, e o jogador agora localiza os agentes próximos com o Focus, uma nova habilidade que destaca detalhes úteis do cenário.
A mudança vem acompanhada da sexta estrela de procurado, ausente em GTA V, e de um sistema que registra o que a polícia sabe sobre a roupa, a aparência, o carro e o parceiro do jogador.
known: Os policiais não aparecem mais como pontos no minimapa; uma área de busca indica onde eles estão procurando.
Ícones abaixo das estrelas mostram o que a polícia sabe, como roupa, aparência, veículo e se havia um cúmplice; uma estrela vazada indica que ela sabe do crime, mas não de quem o cometeu.
Os crimes só são denunciados se uma testemunha vê ou se um alarme dispara.
Trocar a roupa inteira ajuda a se livrar da descrição; óculos escuros ou boné não bastam, e uma máscara durante um assalto pode manter o rosto desconhecido.
O nível de procurado vai até seis estrelas, uma a mais do que em GTA V.
unknown: Uma prévia citou opções de HUD, incluindo um modo de minimapa clássico, mas a Rockstar não disse se alguma configuração volta a mostrar os policiais.
Não foi detalhado por quanto tempo a polícia guarda uma descrição nem como o indicador de câmeras funciona na prática.
A Rockstar não explicou o que ativa as seis estrelas nem como a polícia age nesse nível.
take: É a mudança de design com mais consequências que a Rockstar mostrou até agora, porque mexe no ciclo que o jogador mais repete. Em GTA V, a perseguição acabava quando você saía dos cones no radar. Em GTA VI, o HUD informa o que a polícia sabe, e não onde ela está, o que troca reflexo por preparação: máscara antes do assalto, roupa reserva no carro, um segundo veículo estacionado por perto.

O risco é o atrito virar tédio numa série que também se vende pelo caos. A Rockstar parece saber disso. Nelson disse que ações dentro das missões não pesam no perfil criminal, e o Focus dá ao jogador um jeito de achar policiais sem que o radar faça o trabalho. Se esse equilíbrio se sustenta ao longo de 80 horas de jogo é o teste de verdade, e não dá para julgar isso a partir de uma demonstração editada. A direção, pelo menos, é coerente.

context: En GTA V, la policía aparecía en el radar con conos de visión, así que escapar era sobre todo cuestión de mantenerse fuera de su campo visual. El Extended Look, estrenado en Netflix el 27 de agosto, mostró que GTA VI abandona ese modelo. Durante una persecución de cuatro estrellas, el minimapa mostraba una zona de búsqueda roja en lugar de cada agente, y el jugador ahora ubica a los policías cercanos con Focus, una nueva habilidad que resalta detalles útiles del entorno.
El cambio llega junto con una sexta estrella de búsqueda, ausente en GTA V, y un sistema que registra lo que la policía sabe sobre la ropa, la apariencia, el auto y el cómplice del jugador.
known: Los policías ya no aparecen como puntos en el minimapa; una zona de búsqueda indica dónde están buscando.

Íconos debajo de las estrellas muestran lo que sabe la policía, como tu ropa, tu apariencia, tu vehículo y si tenías un cómplice; una estrella hueca indica que sabe del delito, pero no quién lo cometió.
Los delitos solo se denuncian si un testigo los ve o se activa una alarma.
Cambiarse toda la ropa ayuda a quitarse la descripción; unos lentes de sol o una gorra no alcanzan, y una máscara durante un golpe puede ocultar tu rostro.
El nivel de búsqueda llega a seis estrellas, una más que en GTA V.
unknown: Un avance mencionó opciones de HUD, incluido un modo de minimapa clásico, pero Rockstar no ha dicho si alguna configuración vuelve a mostrar a los agentes.
No se ha detallado cuánto tiempo conserva la policía una descripción ni cómo funciona en la práctica el indicador de cámaras.
Rockstar no ha explicado qué activa las seis estrellas ni cómo actúa la policía en ese nivel.
take: Es el cambio de diseño con más consecuencias que Rockstar ha mostrado hasta ahora, porque toca el ciclo que el jugador más repite. En GTA V, una persecución terminaba al salir de los conos del radar. En GTA VI, el HUD informa lo que sabe la policía y no dónde está, lo que cambia reflejos por preparación: una máscara antes del golpe, ropa de repuesto en el auto, un segundo vehículo estacionado cerca.

El riesgo es que la fricción se vuelva tedio en una serie que también se vende por el caos. Rockstar parece consciente de ello. Nelson dijo que lo que haces dentro de las misiones no cuenta para el perfil criminal, y Focus te da una forma de encontrar policías sin que el radar haga el trabajo. Si ese equilibrio aguanta a lo largo de 80 horas de juego es la verdadera prueba, y no se puede juzgar con una demostración editada. La dirección, al menos, es coherente.

The GTA 6 Extended Look, shown on Netflix in August 2026, made one thing clear: Rockstar has completely redesigned the game's HUD, and the change hits hardest where veterans feel it most — escaping the police.

For years, the trick in Grand Theft Auto was simple: watch the minimap, avoid the red dots and their vision cones, and wait for the stars to fade. In GTA 6, that safety net is gone.

Check out the main changes to the wanted system's HUD:

  • No more "all-seeing" minimap:
    The classic red dots showing each officer's exact position and line of sight have disappeared. Instead, a flashing red-and-blue zone marks the general area where the police are searching for you. Rockstar calls this state Heat.

  • Hanger icon — your clothes:
    Shows that the police know what you are wearing. Changing outfits becomes a real way to throw them off.

  • Face icon — your identity:
    Shows whether a witness or a security camera has identified you, or whether a mask kept your face hidden.

  • Vehicle icon — your getaway car:
    Lets you know if the cops or cameras have identified the car you are using.

  • Partner icon — your accomplice:
    Shows whether the police know you had someone with you during the crime, which matters in a game built around Jason and Lucia working as a pair.

In practice, the HUD now tells you what the police know, not where they are. To find officers, you have to look around, use cover and blend into traffic. Rockstar's Rob Nelson later added in an interview with Famitsu that crimes depend on witnesses, while the Extended Look, shown on August 27, revealed a wanted meter with room for six stars.

It is a big shift for a series that made fleeing the cops almost routine. Expect getaways to take more planning: masks, a change of clothes and a backup car may be as important as a fast engine. For tips on how to lose the police based on everything Rockstar has shown, read our guide: the GTA 6 wanted system.

GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges!

titulo: The GTA 6 Effect: PS5 Pro Sells Out Across the US and Console Sales Jump After the Extended Look
texto: Grand Theft Auto VI isn't out yet, but it is already moving the hardware market. Since the **Extended Look** premiered on Netflix in late August 2026, demand for consoles has spiked, and the **PS5 Pro** has become the hardest machine to find in the United States. By mid-September, the PS5 Pro was listed as out of stock at Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, Target and PlayStation Direct, with GameStop offering only limited pre-owned units in some locations. Check out the main numbers behind the "GTA 6 effect": - **Official price vs. resale:** The PS5 Pro officially costs **$899.99**, after Sony raised it from $749.99 in an increase announced on March 27, 2026 and effective April 2, citing "continued pressures in the global economic landscape" (the press linked the hike to higher memory costs). Third-party sellers took advantage of the shortage, with listings above $1,300 on Amazon and one Walmart marketplace listing asking **$1,469**, roughly 60% above the official price. - **Sales spike in the UK:** According to NielsenIQ data reported by The Game Business, PlayStation 5 sales in the UK rose about **33%** and Xbox Series X|S sales about **34%** in the week after the Extended Look. - **Not just PlayStation:** Xbox consoles saw the same boost, which makes sense: GTA 6 launches only on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with no PC version announced. Analysts urge caution, though. Newzoo's Ronan Patrick noted that a short-term spike does not guarantee lasting growth in console ownership, especially with hardware prices this high. Our advice: if you still need a console for launch day, buy from official retailers and avoid inflated marketplace listings. Restocks tend to arrive in waves as November approaches. Not sure which edition of the game to get? Read our guide: [GTA 6 editions, prices and pre-orders](https://vvviceversa.com/guides/gta-6-editions-prices-pre-order/). GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges! *Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article said the PS5 Pro's price rose from $699 and that Sony cited higher memory costs. In fact, it rose from $749.99 to $899.99 (announced March 27, effective April 2, 2026), and Sony cited global economic pressures; the link to memory costs was the press's reading.*

context: GTA VI is arriving at an awkward moment for console prices. Sony raised US prices on March 27, 2026, with the PS5 Pro going from $749.99 to $899.99 from April 2, its second increase in under a year, and Microsoft added $150 to Xbox Series X|S prices from August 1. In June, The Game Business already reported that retailers expected console shortages around the November 19 launch.
The Netflix showcase, watched by more than 30 million people, then gave UK sales a short boost against a weak year: UK console sales were down 14.4% year on year through July, with PS5 down 32%.
known: In the UK, PS5 sales rose 33% and Xbox Series X|S sales 34% in the week after the August 27 Extended Look, according to NielsenIQ data reported by The Game Business.
The PS5 Pro costs $899.99 in the US after an increase announced on March 27, 2026; Sony cited “continued pressures in the global economic landscape.”
By late August, PS5 Pro stock had sold out at Best Buy, Walmart, Target and PlayStation Direct in the US.
Newzoo's Ronan Patrick expects GTA VI and Call of Duty to lift the console install base, but “nothing particularly massive.”
unknown: Whether the UK jump lasted beyond a single week; the published data covers only the reveal week.
How much stock Sony and Microsoft have set aside for November; Sony told investors in May it had secured “the necessary volume” for 2026, without giving numbers.
How much of the PS5 Pro shortage comes from GTA VI demand and how much from tight supply, which retailers were already warning about in June.
take: A 33% weekly jump sounds dramatic, but it comes off a low base. UK console sales were falling sharply before the Extended Look, and one strong week does not reverse that. Newzoo's view, an uptick but nothing massive, fits the numbers better than the “GTA 6 effect” headlines, ours included. The PS5 Pro shortage is real, but it also reflects constrained supply: retailers were warning about year-end shortages in June, before anyone had seen the gameplay.

For players, price is the bigger story. At $899.99, the PS5 Pro costs $150 more than it did in March, and Sony justified that in broad economic terms, not by pointing to GTA. Paying a reseller's markup on top of that makes little sense when the standard PS5 and Xbox Series X|S will run the same game on November 19. If you need hardware for launch, buying at list price and accepting a short wait for a restock is the more sensible plan.

titulo_es: Efecto GTA 6: la PS5 Pro se agota en EE. UU. y las ventas de consolas se disparan tras el Extended Look
texto_es: Grand Theft Auto VI aún no ha salido, pero ya está moviendo el mercado de consolas. Desde el estreno del **Extended Look** en Netflix a finales de agosto de 2026, la demanda se ha disparado, y la **PS5 Pro** se ha convertido en la consola más difícil de encontrar en Estados Unidos. A mediados de septiembre, la PS5 Pro figuraba como agotada en Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, Target y PlayStation Direct, y GameStop solo ofrecía algunas unidades de segunda mano en tiendas concretas. Estas son las cifras clave del "efecto GTA 6": - **Precio oficial frente a reventa:** La PS5 Pro cuesta oficialmente **899,99 dólares** en EE. UU., después de que Sony subiera su precio desde 749,99 dólares, en un aumento anunciado el 27 de marzo de 2026 y vigente desde el 2 de abril, alegando "presiones continuas en el panorama económico global" (la prensa lo vinculó al mayor costo de la memoria). Los revendedores aprovecharon la escasez, con anuncios de más de 1.300 dólares en Amazon y uno en el marketplace de Walmart que pedía **1.469 dólares**, alrededor de un 60 % por encima del precio oficial. - **Ventas al alza en Reino Unido:** Según datos de NielsenIQ publicados por The Game Business, las ventas de PlayStation 5 en Reino Unido subieron alrededor de un **33 %** y las de Xbox Series X|S un **34 %** en la semana posterior al Extended Look. - **No solo PlayStation:** Las consolas Xbox recibieron el mismo impulso, algo lógico: GTA 6 solo sale en PS5 y Xbox Series X|S, sin versión de PC anunciada. Los analistas piden prudencia. Ronan Patrick, de Newzoo, señaló que un pico a corto plazo no garantiza un crecimiento duradero del parque de consolas, sobre todo con precios tan altos. Nuestro consejo: si aún necesitas una consola para el lanzamiento, compra en tiendas oficiales y evita los anuncios inflados. Las reposiciones suelen llegar por oleadas a medida que se acerca noviembre. ¿Dudas sobre qué edición del juego comprar?
